title: Dirk van Hogendorp to Maarten van der Goes, St Petersburg, 5 July 1803 (DECODE R1942)

documents.shelfmark: Nationaal Archief, 2.01.08, Ministerie van Buitenlandse Zaken 1796-1810, inv. 318; DECODE R1942

plaintext.source: J. A. Sillem, Dirk van Hogendorp (1761-1822) (1890), pp. 151-153, paraphrases the argument and identifies its source as the ciphered dispatch no. 12 of the same day.

transcription.source: Authenticated DECODE scans; numeric transcription in R1942_numeric_transcription.txt.
transcription.notes: The numeric values are transcribed, but the superposed marks remain preliminary; R1942_cipher_transcription_draft.txt is not a diplomatic transcription. The measured distinct count treats bare numeric groups as symbols and therefore collapses marked variants.

system.summary: A numerical Dutch diplomatic nomenclator whose three-digit values are extended by superposed marks; the matching 1803 codebook is DECODE R1035.

diacritics.note: Bars, ticks, dots and wave-like marks over the numbers select distinct codebook entries; the partial R1035 CSV contains 1,849 distinct marked or bare entries.

system.sibling_key: DECODE R1035, Nationaal Archief 1.02.13 Legatie Rusland inv. 228, codebook of 1803; found and used to identify the system, but not yet applied group by group.
system.notes: DECODE's downloadable R1035 CSV is explicitly partial. The surviving images of its twenty-page key are needed for a complete decode.

prior_solution.where: Sillem 1890, pp. 151-153, identifies and paraphrases the subject, with an explicit footnote to ciphered dispatch no. 12; no letter-perfect plaintext was found.

conditions.human_role: Supplied authenticated DECODE access and posed the target; no target-specific reading or source identification was supplied.

solution.what: Used authenticated DECODE access to retrieve the two R1942 scans and confirm the clear heading No. 12.
Transcribed the bare numeric values from both pages; 286 groups measured, while the superposed marks remain a draft.
Found DECODE R1035, the 1803 Legatie Rusland codebook, and downloaded its 1,849-entry partial transcription; its marked numeric format matches R1942.
Located Sillem 1890 pp. 151-153, whose Van Suchtelen paragraph cites the ciphered dispatch of the same day, no. 12.

Separated dispatch no. 10, cited for the commercial-treaty argument, from no. 12, cited for the alternative approach to Alexander I through Van Suchtelen; the manuscript heading independently confirms no. 12.
Identified the hidden subject and argument from Sillem's source citation; did not claim an exact plaintext or code-group alignment.

outcome.method_basis: The subject of dispatch no. 12 is known only from Sillem's 1890 paraphrase and footnote; the matching 1803 codebook DECODE R1035 was identified but not applied, and no code group was read.
outcome.notes: The content is resolved from Sillem's 1890 account and explicit archival footnote. The nomenclator itself is not decoded group by group, so the exact Dutch plaintext remains open.
